newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany wants strong, large currency union - Dini.
newsitem.headline: Germany wants strong, large currency union - Dini.

text.p: Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said on Friday that Germany wanted a strong and large European monetary union and that relations between Rome and Bonn remained excellent.
"Germany believes in a strong and large European currency union," he told reporters on the sidelines of talks between Italian and German ministers in Bonn.
Dini also said Bonn and Rome enjoyed "excellent relations". "We are sorry there are those who try to destroy this but they will not succeed," he said.

Dini is accompanying Prime Minister Romano Prodi , in Bonn for talks with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl which were likely to touch on Italy's chances of joining the planned currency union at its scheduled launch in 1999.

Italy has been irritated by speculation that Germany was unwilling to allow southern European nations into the currency union at the start as their efforts to tidy up their finances had not gone far enough.

Dini said reports, such as one in Britain's Financial Times this week, suggesting there was a plan to delay Italian entry into the single currency had been caused by people who were neither competent nor authorised to discuss the issue.
Italy has stressed that it intends to be among the first nations to join the currency union.
